dublinCore.title: Complex Plane
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Complex numbers
Signal processing
Phasors
Polar form
Rectangular form
dublinCore.description: Interactive visualization of complex numbers in the complex plane showing both rectangular (a + bi) and polar (r angle theta) forms with geometric representations including magnitude, phase, and projections.

learningObjectives: Identify the real part a on the blue horizontal axis and the imaginary part b on the red vertical axis for a plotted complex number z
Calculate the magnitude |z| as the square root of a squared plus b squared, using the right triangle drawn beneath the green vector
Calculate the phase angle theta as the arctangent of b over a, and locate it as the green arc from the positive real axis
Convert between the rectangular form a + bi and the polar form r at angle theta shown in the two information panels
Predict how changing only the real part moves the vector's tip, its magnitude, and its phase angle

misconceptions.misconception: The phase angle is always arctan(b/a) with no quadrant adjustment
misconceptions.correction: arctan alone cannot distinguish opposite quadrants; the angle must be placed in the quadrant where the point lies
misconceptions.evidence: Move the point into quadrant II or III and watch the green arc sweep past 90 degrees even though b/a changes sign only once

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Interactive complex plane. Two sliders set the real and imaginary parts of z. The display shows the vector from the origin to z, its magnitude, its phase angle, and both rectangular and polar forms.

controls.label: Real Part (a)
controls.description: Sets Re(z), the horizontal coordinate of the complex number

controls.label: Imaginary Part (b)
controls.description: Sets Im(z), the vertical coordinate of the complex number

visualElements.description: Argand diagram with real axis (blue), imaginary axis (red) and the complex number vector (green)
Left panel with Re(z), Im(z), |z| and theta; right panel with rectangular and polar forms

model.description: Maps (a, b) to magnitude r = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) and phase theta = atan2(b, a)

extensions: Add a second complex number and show the sum and product geometrically
